title: Boundaries 2: Test Colons and Dashes
description: After full-stop choices fail, test colons and then single or paired dashes. Use a clear yes/no test for each job, choose a passing answer, and stop.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: At dawn the staff packed three ______ rope, tarps, and lanterns.
questions.explanation_html: The text before the blank is a complete statement. The ending specifies what that statement anticipates, so a colon introduces the explanation.
questions.variation: After a complete lead-in, use a colon to specify what follows

distractor_notes.B: Requires a complete independent clause on the right.
distractor_notes.C: Adds a conjunction where the ending does not contain a full clause.
distractor_notes.D: Leaves the explanation without a boundary.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The volunteer counted ______ six damaged chairs before requesting replacements.
questions.explanation_html: The verb needs the object that follows it. The portion ending at the blank does not make a complete statement on its own, so keep the verb attached to its object.
questions.variation: Keep a verb attached to its required object

distractor_notes.A: Separates text that needs to stay in one clause.
distractor_notes.B: Separates text that needs to stay in one clause.
distractor_notes.C: Makes an unfinished phrase stand on its own.
